requirements.summary: Executor wrote /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf with 'blacklist usb-storage' and 'install usb-storage /bin/false'. Immediately after, 'modprobe usb-storage' failed and lsmod confirmed the module was not loaded, directly demonstrating the module is blocked from loading now.

requirements.requirement: Block usb-storage from loading after a reboot (persistence)
requirements.summary: Config file was bundled into a regenerated initramfs (dracut -f --regenerate-all, confirmed file present inside initramfs). After an actual reboot (boot_id changed from 6aa805ba... to 15ba9cd1...), the blacklist file still existed, modprobe usb-storage still failed with the same install-command error, and modprobe --showconfig showed the blacklist/install directives for usb_storage as active. This is a full pre-restart baseline, restart, and post-restart verification of the actual persisted behavior.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied both material outcomes of the task: usb-storage is blocked from loading immediately via modprobe blacklist/install directives, and persistence across reboot was directly demonstrated with a pre-restart baseline, an actual observed reboot (boot_id change), and post-restart verification showing the module still blocked and the configuration still active via modprobe --showconfig. The mandatory node1 restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently captured (healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered healthy state with no failed services). No unnecessary mutations or residue were found.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled for this task), so preparer-vs-executor differentiation relies solely on the executor_comparison against before_prepare, which is adequate here.
modprobe --showconfig output was truncated in the evidence capture, but the header and relevant blacklist/install lines for usb_storage were visible and sufficient to confirm the directive is active.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor commands were either read-only diagnostics, the necessary configuration write, the necessary initramfs rebuild for persistence, or the mandatory restart/verification sequence. The reboot (cmd-e2332f2f06d241cd) is a necessary state-changing action directly tied to verifying persistence, and boot-identity/socket/PID changes seen in the after_executor snapshot (new sshd/chronyd PIDs, new systemd-private tmp dirs, /tmp/reboot.log) are all expected, non-residue side effects of a normal reboot rather than executor-introduced clutter. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations, no failed services, and package health remained consistent (manager=dnf) before and after. /tmp/reboot.log is a trivial artifact of the backgrounded reboot command but is negligible, non-sensitive, and does not affect functionality.
